items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-02
items.q: But if I wrote a letter to Don Albert, Albert Dominique in San Antonio at that time, you would have nowhere to get it.

ctx.x: sort of constrained and stiff in manner and never was willing to talk a lot that I could get out of them. We were always very awkward with each other. Certainly I thought the records he put out under his label were very interesting and very good. I still have a number of them. And what little I've read of his writings I enjoyed but Bill was always difficult for me to talk to so I just didn't talk to him or he didn't talk to me much or something of the sort. Were there many people in the

shop? Musicians or music lovers? Usually when I went by. But you know you have to test them. Yes, I see something tiny. Yeah, but you know this part of it it doesn't pick up. Right here? Yeah, the very beginning doesn't always pick up. But it's going now. Today is what? Today is the Food. August 3rd, 1978. And we're at 5th at, no I'm getting it wrong, not 15. Our address? 715 St. James. St. James. And I have to get you all to give your names. Your right name. Dine Albert. Herbert Hall. Is that your full name? It…
I don't know. Herb is, it's just Herbert, you know. And no middle name at all, huh? No. You don't use that name? Well I use it in the Union but I don't use it as well.
